channel.title: Hypewire
channel.description: What people are talking about in AI, entertainment, gaming and tech, refreshed daily.

item.title: Sunrise on the Reaping takes $56 million on Friday, heading for $120 million
item.description: The Hunger Games prequel made a reported $56 million on its first day and is projected at about $120 million in the US and $200 million worldwide.

item.title: GTA VI makes $3.79 billion on day one, Rockstar says
item.description: Rockstar says Grand Theft Auto VI took $3.79 billion in first-day worldwide retail sales, and 32.5 million copies were pre-sold.

item.title: Nasdaq drops 5.3% as the AI trade cracks in its worst week since April 2025
item.description: The Nasdaq fell 5.28% on November 20, wiping out its gains for 2026, as AI stocks led a sell-off in the week of Anthropic's market debut.

item.title: Nvidia falls 13% after a report of an SEC look at its accounting
item.description: Nvidia shares fell 13% on November 20 after Reuters reported SEC enforcement staff are examining possible accounting issues at the company.

item.title: Anthropic shares give back most of their debut gains on day two
item.description: Anthropic stock closed about 9% lower on November 20 after a strong debut, as heavy trading turned over more shares than the IPO sold.

item.title: Extortion group claims leak of Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan customer data
item.description: A group called n0n claims it stole data tied to Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan, and the banks say marketing data at vendors was exposed.

item.title: US and China agree humans must stay in charge of military AI, Bessent says
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Trump and Xi agreed that no major military operation should be launched by AI without a human involved.

item.title: Hackers used AI agents to find a zero-day in a medical imaging server, Amazon says
item.description: Amazon says suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to find an unknown flaw in MONAI Label and take over a university server.

item.title: Apple is said to be building an AI agent that can run your Mac
item.description: Bloomberg reports Apple is working on an agent that could control Mac apps, browse the web and write code, based on a job listing it later removed.

item.title: US approved over 879,000 AI chips for Chinese firms, House records show
item.description: A House committee released licence records showing Commerce approved more than 879,000 AI chip sales to Chinese companies as of May 2026.

item.title: YouTube pulls and warns GTA VI streams over nudity, then backs age limits
item.description: Some GTA VI streamers had channels removed or warned by YouTube over nudity, before YouTube said age restrictions were the right step, Notebookcheck reports.

item.title: Anthropic says Claude Mythos cut AMD GPU setup from months to days
item.description: Anthropic says Claude Mythos cut the software work to bring up AMD GPUs from up to 12 months to around three days, writing almost all kernels itself.

item.title: Google's new search homepage shows AI chat history and drops the search button
item.description: Google is rolling out a redesigned search homepage that shows AI chat history and has no search button, Ars Technica reports.

item.title: Oracle says its OpenAI contract is fully funded as shares slip below its offer price
item.description: Oracle said it has secured all the funding needed for its OpenAI contract, while its stock closed at $101.19, below the $116 price of new shares it sold.

item.title: Twitch calls GTA VI its largest game launch ever
item.description: Twitch says GTA VI was its biggest game launch, with 3.3 million viewers at once, Bloomberg reports. StreamCharts counted nearly 8 million in all.

item.title: Bell Canada says an AI agent-driven hacker stole enterprise customer data
item.description: Bell Canada confirmed that an 'agentic' threat actor breached its systems on November 17 and stole data on enterprise customers, BleepingComputer reports.

item.title: Apollo and Goldman price about $44 billion of notes to buy GPUs for SpaceX
item.description: Apollo and Goldman Sachs priced roughly $44 billion of notes to buy Nvidia chips and equipment for SpaceX, Reuters reports.

item.title: GTA VI's Metacritic user score opens at 5.2, raising review-bombing claims
item.description: GTA VI's user score on Metacritic opened at 5.2 out of 10, far below its 99 critic score, prompting accusations of review bombing, Notebookcheck reports.

item.title: California's attorney general subpoenas Nvidia over chips and China
item.description: AG Rob Bonta served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena asking whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China.

item.title: Researchers show a webpage could make Meta's Muse leak private chats
item.description: Researchers showed a malicious webpage could pull a Meta Muse user's private chats, memories and stored account logins without any prompt.

item.title: Databricks is said to be in talks to raise money at about $225 billion
item.description: Databricks is in early talks to raise several billion dollars at a valuation of about $225 billion, the Wall Street Journal reports.

item.title: I Play Rocky places second as it goes nationwide
item.description: Amazon MGM's Stallone biopic I Play Rocky ran second behind the Hunger Games prequel in its first wide weekend, Cover Media reports.

item.title: BADBOX botnet returns on cheap Android TV boxes with 40 billion ad requests a day
item.description: The BADBOX malware found on generic Android TV boxes is back running ad fraud at a record 40 billion ad requests a day, BleepingComputer reports.

item.title: EU Commission confirms a cyberattack that used an AI hacking tool
item.description: The European Commission says attackers disrupted its systems for over 10 days, and CERT-EU says they used an AI penetration-testing tool named ARTEX.

item.title: AMD powers over 40% of the new TOP500 supercomputer list
item.description: AMD now appears in more than 40% of the systems on the new TOP500 list, and its Lux system with the US Department of Energy debuts at No. 14.

item.title: Yellowjackets begins its final season on Paramount+
item.description: The fourth and final 10-episode season of Yellowjackets premiered on November 20, with the finale set for January 22, 2027, Forbes reports.

item.title: Percy Jackson and the Olympians season 3 premieres on Disney+
item.description: The third season of the Percy Jackson series arrived on Disney+ and Hulu on November 20, leading the weekend's streaming picks.

item.title: Ubisoft is down 1,100 staff in six months as it launches an AI subsidiary
item.description: After cutting 166 more jobs in Montreal and Quebec City, Ubisoft is down about 1,100 staff in six months and has set up an AI unit called Motherbrain.

item.title: A Persona 6 website update fuels talk of a Game Awards trailer
item.description: Fans spotted an update to a Persona 6 web domain, sparking speculation that Atlus will show a trailer at The Game Awards on December 10.

item.title: Nvidia unveils Rubin HPC, a GPU with over 50,000 CUDA cores, for 2028
item.description: Nvidia announced Rubin HPC at the SC26 conference, a Rubin GPU variant for scientific simulation and AI agent workloads arriving in 2028.

item.title: Trump says US firms building AI data centers abroad could face taxes
item.description: President Trump said at a White House news conference that companies building AI facilities overseas could face substantial taxes or restrictions.

item.title: Obsession, a $400 million hit made for $750,000, arrives on Netflix
item.description: The 2026 film Obsession, which reportedly grossed more than $400 million on a $750,000 budget, is now streaming on Netflix.

item.title: Nintendo's winter catalogue gives a first glimpse of Pokemon Winds and Waves
item.description: Nintendo's Japanese Winter Catalogue includes a short description of Pokemon Winds and Waves, promising islands and a vast ocean to explore.

item.title: WhatsApp patches three flaws, including one it suspects was used in scams
item.description: Meta's WhatsApp fixed three security flaws, including an Android bug in ad-reply links that it suspects was used in scam messages.

item.title: Valve drops Steam Machine waitlists, blaming memory and storage costs
item.description: Valve says it will stop running Steam Machine waitlists because it does not know how many it can make or what they will cost.

item.title: Netflix releases Steps, an animated film with Ali Wong and Amanda Seyfried
item.description: Steps, a new animated feature voiced by Ali Wong and Amanda Seyfried, joined Netflix on November 20 as a top pick of the weekend.

item.title: Switch 2 was the best-selling US console in October, with Modern Warfare 4 the top game
item.description: Nintendo Switch 2 was the top-selling console in the US in October 2026, and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 was the best-selling game, MyNintendoNews reports.

item.title: Ebenezer slips to third in its second weekend
item.description: Johnny Depp's Ebenezer fell to third in its second weekend behind the Hunger Games prequel and I Play Rocky, Cover Media reports.

item.title: SNL takes a Thanksgiving break and returns December 5 with Amanda Seyfried
item.description: Saturday Night Live had no new episode on November 21 and will return on December 5 with Amanda Seyfried hosting and Don Toliver as musical guest.

item.title: A24's Anthony Bourdain biopic Tony starts streaming on HBO Max
item.description: Tony, the 2026 A24 film about chef and TV host Anthony Bourdain, is now streaming on HBO Max, Boston.com reports.

item.title: European streamer SkyShowtime will shut down at the end of 2027
item.description: SkyShowtime, a joint venture of Comcast's Sky and Paramount Skydance, will close at the end of 2027, with its CEO leaving, Deadline reports.

item.title: Sony misses a Game Awards GOTY nomination for the first time in 12 years
item.description: None of Marvel's Wolverine, Saros or Marathon made The Game Awards' Game of the Year list, ending Sony's 12-year run of nominations.

item.title: TT Games' teased LEGO City Undercover announcement turns out to be a map
item.description: TT Games promised a LEGO City Undercover announcement for November 20, and it turned out to be a downloadable world map of the game.
